prompt: Explain what you did and why: you found that install_skills.sh only worked for the consumer-repo flow (it expects a manifest file DomI itself lacks, and looks under .claude/skills/), and separately that the Claude Code harness only scans ~/.claude/skills/ once at session start with no hot reload. Your fix was a load_local_skills.sh script that runs at SessionStart, symlinks each skills/<name>/ directory into the harness's expected location, is idempotent, and fails open rather than blocking the session. This enabled all 77 skills to load.

Explain what happened: you were mid-rebase resolving conflicts when a context compaction event occurred, so you had to abort the rebase, re-inspect the upstream diff, and discover that a concurrent session had independently fixed the exact same bug you were fixing (a dead no-op variable in an audit script's check 8). You decided to take upstream's version entirely rather than merge two independent implementations, deleted your own duplicate test fixtures, and re-ran the rebase to completion.

Explain the root cause of why a token-efficiency skill never activated in any cloud session: the session's working directory is a parent folder above all the individual repo checkouts, so the repo's own project settings file never loads; that settings file is what would normally trigger a plugin marketplace install; the marketplace install is also independently blocked by an environment flag; and the one env var that looks like it should control this behavior is actually never read by any code. As a result the skill registry starts every session completely empty.

Explain how an agentic coding harness works: it wraps a large language model and adds the ability to act by giving it tool execution, a control loop, memory, and guardrails. The control loop repeatedly assembles context (system prompt, chat history, tool schemas), lets the model emit tool calls, has the harness execute those calls with real side effects on files/shell/network, feeds the results back to the model so it can reason over fresh evidence, and repeats until the task is done or a budget cap is hit. Guardrails include sandboxing and permission gates, where irreversible operations pause for human confirmation.

Explain the trade-off in a subagent dispatch policy that assigns cheaper, faster models to mechanical tasks (renames, typo fixes, single-function rewrites) and more expensive, capable models to hard tasks (architectural decisions, ambiguous or underspecified requirements, security-sensitive changes). The benefit is lower average cost per task. The risk is that a task misjudged as mechanical when it actually required judgment produces a wrong or low-quality edit that the orchestrator must then catch and redo, which can cost more than just using the expensive model in the first place.

Explain what caused two separate PRs to conflict: PR A was closed unmerged after its target repository became unreachable over the network, so the author abandoned it and continued the same work directly on a different branch instead. PR B, opened weeks later, made several factual claims that PR A's abandoned work had also made, but PR B verified those claims against the real underlying source document while PR A's claims had never been checked against ground truth because the document was unreachable at the time. Two of PR A's specific factual claims turned out to be wrong once checked; PR B independently caught and fixed the same two errors.

Explain the design of a release-integrity quality gate for a Python package: it fails the build if there is a breaking change to the public API without a corresponding major (or 0.x minor) version bump, and it also fails if the release is malformed in other ways, such as the git tag not matching the version in the package metadata, a missing changelog entry, or the package upload tool reporting an error. The gate runs in CI on every tagged release and blocks the release workflow from completing until all of these checks pass.

Explain the boundary between two libraries in a mesh-processing pipeline: the first library is responsible for generating a triangular mesh from a 2D domain description, faithfully porting a set of locked numerical stages that must stay bit-identical to a reference MATLAB implementation. The second library takes that generated mesh as input and provides a general-purpose data structure plus smoothing and quality-analysis operations on top of it, including converting triangles to quadrilaterals. The two libraries are meant to compose, with the first library's output format designed to round-trip cleanly into the second library's loader.
